editorial.headline: A Closed Category for Prohibited Narcotic and Medicinal Plants
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the cultivation cycle for narcotic and prohibited medicinal plants, but it is closed to foreign ownership nationally and blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This KBLI activity is not a broad agricultural category. It is a tightly defined classification for the farming of narcotic plants and prohibited medicinal plants. The scope covers the full cultivation chain when handled as one integrated activity: land preparation, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest work. In plain English, the code is about growing these restricted plants, not simply trading, researching, or processing them as a separate business line.

The record says the activity is open across all business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That means the scale field does not narrow the classification to one size of operator. A small operation and a large operation can both fall inside the same activity description if the underlying work is the farming cycle described in the scope. The important point is that scale openness is not the same as foreign-ownership openness. For founders, those two ideas need to be read separately.

On foreign ownership, the national position is absolute. The PMA status is TERTUTUP and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%. There is no partial foreign stake to structure around in this record. The source cited is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021, and the practical reading is direct: this is not a foreign-owned setup category at the national level. The code may describe an activity that exists in the classification system, and it may be open across micro through large scale bands, but it is closed for PMA ownership.

Bali does not soften that answer. Its L4 Bali status is also TERTUTUP, and the record marks it as blocked. The stated Bali reason is that the activity is closed to foreign ownership at the national level, with a 0% ceiling. On top of that, the Bali moratorium rule in the record says the province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. The honest editorial conclusion is therefore simple: a foreigner cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali. The national rule already closes the door, and the Bali status confirms that the door is closed locally as well.
editorial.pullQuote: Scale openness does not change the central fact: this activity carries a 0% foreign-ownership ceiling and is blocked for PMA in Bali.
